findings.title: Slot grid shows "Few left" slots in a separate block above the Morning heading, out of DOM and time order
findings.description: Under 1.3.2 the reading order a screen reader or keyboard follows should match the order the page presents visually. In the DOM and the ARIA snapshot every slot sits in time order under the 'Morning' or 'Afternoon' heading (08:00, 08:20 Few left, 08:40 Few left ...). On screen, every 'Few left' slot from both halves of the day is moved into one block above the 'Morning' heading (on Saturday 17: 08:20, 08:40, 09:00, 09:40, 10:20, 10:40, 13:40, 14:00, 15:00, 16:40). Below that block, 'Morning' shows only 08:00, 09:20, 10:00 and the full slots. So the visual grouping (Morning/Afternoon), the time order and the DOM order disagree, at 320 px and at 1280 px. Afternoon slots such as 13:40 appear above the Morning heading. The keyboard check's 08:00 to 08:20 inversion is one symptom; this record covers the meaning: the heading structure the snapshot exposes does not match what sighted users see.

criteria.name: Match between system and the real world

findings.impact: Residents who use a screen reader together with sight (low vision, larger text), or a keyboard, may hear or tab through a sequence that does not match the grid they see, and may misread a 'Few left' afternoon slot as a morning slot. That makes it harder to book the right 20-minute slot, which is the scarce resource here.

findings.title: Chosen day and chosen slot are marked only by a pale tint and slightly heavier border
findings.description: Selected 'Saturday 17' and slot '09:20' differ from unselected tiles by a light green fill (#e3f2eb on white) and a slightly thicker border; at a glance the chosen slot is about as prominent as the greyed Full tiles.
findings.recommendation: Decide how strongly the chosen state should differ from free and Full, given the slot is the scarce thing the resident is committing to.

findings.title: Date repeated twice under 'Slots'
findings.description: Under 'Slots' the page states 'Saturday 17 October' and then '22 slots free on Saturday 17 October' as two separate lines, adding a third and fourth line of grey text before the grid.
findings.recommendation: Decide which single line carries the chosen day and the free count.

findings.title: No identity layer: the frame is a portable council form
findings.description: Across all four surfaces the only identity is 'Dunmore District Council' in bold body text and a small bin glyph; type, colour, tiles and cards are the category default. The recycling centre, the yard and the gate leave no visual trace; the done-page reference is bold text in a white card.
findings.impact: Design note: 'plain, not bare' asks for an identity floor; the pages read bare.
findings.recommendation: Decide one element from the centre's own world (the gate pass, the site, the waste streams) that carries identity quietly on every step, starting with the done-page reference.

findings.title: Vehicle chips and day chips are drawn as two different control styles
findings.description: Day chips on the when screen use green bold labels with green borders; vehicle chips on the next step use black regular labels with grey borders, though both are single-choice segmented controls.
findings.impact: Design note: a small coherence lapse between consecutive steps.
findings.recommendation: Decide one treatment for single-choice chips and use it on both steps.

findings.title: Two day chips look selected at 375
findings.description: At 375 in light and dark, with Saturday 17 chosen, the 'Tomorrow' chip also carries the tinted selection fill, close to the selected 'Saturday 17' (which differs only by a heavier border). At 1440 only Saturday is tinted. It may be a hover or focus residue in the capture.
findings.impact: The chosen day is the first decision; the selected state should be unambiguous.

evidence.detail: 'Tomorrow' and 'Saturday 17' both have the pale green fill

findings.recommendation: Confirm whether this is a captured hover state; either way, decide a selected treatment that differs from hover by more than border weight.

findings.title: Sterile default: no own element on when, vehicle and confirm ('plain, not bare' tips into bare)
findings.description: Pale ground, thin borders on white boxes, one sans, no focal point after the H1 and nothing the product owns; the identity is the council name and a small bin icon. DESIGN.md asks for 'plain, not bare'.
findings.recommendation: Decide one element that carries 'civic' and 'plain, not bare' on purpose (the slot, the reference, or the masthead) and give it the care the rest of the page does not need.
